source.title: Towards Backward-Compatible Representation Learning
source.authors: Yan-Tao Shen; Yuanjun Xiong; W. Xia; Stefano Soatto

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices and references; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: It tests direct cross-model use with downstream recognition metrics rather than measuring representational distance or similarity. The independently trained model comparisons bear on whether representations work interchangeably without an alignment procedure.
record.gate_note: The independent-model comparisons are uninduced direct-compatibility results and are recorded. Results for BCT, L2 regularization, and other training procedures intentionally trained for compatibility are not evidence that models show interchangeability without that inducement, so they are not used as claim-version rows or verdict evidence.
record.test_reason: The study proposes backward-compatible training (BCT), which induces compatibility on purpose. Its only uninduced result is a sanity check that compares independently trained face and person-search embeddings directly, with no mapping, stitching or relative representation. V4 is about whether a simple, usually learned, map makes representations interchangeable. Direct comparison in raw coordinates cannot show that, because independently trained embeddings are expected to differ by an arbitrary basis even if they are mappable. The paper cites the Convergent Learning paper (an original source) only as a related experiment. No version is tested. The independent-model results go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. BCT yields backward-compatible embeddings with small accuracy loss, works across most architecture, dimension and loss changes (failing with Softmax-to-CosFace and an added ReLU), and supports transitive chain updates. Independently trained models are not naturally compatible.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes backward-compatible training using an old model's classifier influence loss and evaluates downstream retrieval compatibility; it does not reproduce a representation-similarity measurement from the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported uninduced compatibility outcomes differ across the tested task and dataset: IJB-C face verification/search versus Market-1501 person search.

fits_no_version.finding: Independently trained face embedding models (ResNet-101, 50% vs 100% of IMDB-Face) give about 0% cross-model accuracy when compared directly without any mapping. A person re-ID pair drops from 42.9 to 26.7 mAP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently trained embedding models are not directly interchangeable in raw coordinates without alignment or compatibility training.

record.problems: Evidence concerns downstream recognition compatibility, not similarity between representation-space distances. The uninduced comparisons are limited to the reported model/data setups and retrieval tasks; cross-modal alignment and other similarity measures are not tested.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Results from BCT and other procedures trained specifically to induce compatibility are excluded from claim-version rows and verdicts because they do not show compatibility arising without that inducement.

untested.parts: No scale sweep and no similarity measurement.
No seed-to-seed feature or subspace analysis.
No uninduced linear map, stitching, relative representation or unpaired mapping. The one linear-transformer attempt was part of BCT training and is not reported quantitatively.
No comparison of similarity measures or input distributions.
No alignment measurement or causal analysis of what drives alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'challenges' label is removed because direct unmapped comparison does not test mappability. Results from BCT, L2 regularization and LwF are induced compatibility and were correctly excluded from claim-version rows.

versions.untested_parts: No scale sweep or measurement of similarity between representations as model size or capability increases.
No vision-language models or paired image-caption representation alignment.
No analysis of shared features or subspaces across random seeds of the same architecture.
Tests direct cross-model retrieval compatibility only; does not test mapping methods, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping methods.
No interpretable features or circuits are identified or compared across models.
Does not compare representation-similarity measures, their settings, or in-distribution versus out-of-distribution inputs.
Does not measure representational alignment or test whether shared data or objectives explain alignment.

rows.subject: (φ∗new, φold)
rows.operation_detail: Measured direct cross-model face-verification performance for independently trained models, using the new model for the first template and the old model for the second.
rows.note: The paper reports almost 0% accuracy in the backward test and marks the pair incompatible. The models differ in training data amount (50% versus 100%); both use the stated default architecture and training setup.
rows.check: Measures direct identity-map retrieval compatibility (0.0 vs 77.86 TAR), not whether a simple map aligns the two embeddings. A raw-coordinate comparison cannot show or refute V4.

rows.subject: (φ∗new, φold)
rows.operation_detail: Measured direct cross-model face-search performance for independently trained models, using the new model for queries and the old model for the gallery.
rows.note: The paper reports almost 0% accuracy in the backward test and marks the pair incompatible. The models differ in training data amount (50% versus 100%); both use the stated default architecture and training setup.
rows.check: Same issue as r1: direct, unmapped 1:N search (0.0 vs 59.34 TPIR) does not measure mappability.

rows.subject: (φold, φ∗new)
rows.operation_detail: Measured direct cross-model person-search performance for models trained without BCT.
rows.note: The new model was trained on 100% of training data and the old model on 50%, both following [40] without BCT. The table marks this comparison incompatible.
rows.check: Direct unmapped person-search comparison (26.7 vs 42.9 mAP) does not measure mappability. Some cross-model retrieval survives here (26.7 is not near zero), so 'absent' also overstates it.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Independently trained model comparisons on IJB-C and Market-1501
reader_labels.reason: Direct cross-model use is reported as incompatible: IJB-C results are 0.0 at the stated operating points, and Market-1501 mean AP is 26.7 versus 42.9 for the old-model reference (r1–r3).
